records.name: Roots Garden Friends Group
records.summary: Neighbors who tend the Roots Garden, a community garden inside Fisher Park in Olney. Older sources describe residents nurturing it for decades, but we could not confirm what it does today.
records.what_you_do: Older sources describe volunteer work days on the third Saturday of each month, when people clean litter, plant, and care for the garden and the park's trees. Confirm before you come, since we could not verify these still run.

schedule.text: Older sources describe work days on the third Saturday of each month. We could not confirm the current schedule.

first_step.how: Email the group at the address on the City's Park Friends list and ask when the next garden work day is. If there is no reply, email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group.

records.notes: The City list gives Fisher Park as the other name. Search results (not opened) describe the garden as part of Fisher Park, cared for with the Fisher Park Community Alliance. The newest of those sources is about 2023, and the exact date is not confirmed. One search summary gives 600 W Spencer Ave for the park itself, while the City list gives 572 W Spencer St, which is used here. No website was found. Not searched further: the WebSearch budget was spent. The Fisher Park Community Alliance is in leads_only.

records.name: Keep Royal Gardens Beautiful
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up, plant, and beautify Morris Park and the Overbrook area, and who work against graffiti and illegal dumping. The group also lists tai chi classes at the park.
records.what_you_do: Help clear invasive plants and dumped trash, plant gardens, and take part in the group's events. The site asks volunteers to commit to at least two times a year. Tai chi classes are listed on weekday mornings.

schedule.text: Tai chi classes (Yang and Ru styles) Tuesday to Friday, 7 to 8 am. The page gives no dates for volunteer days.

first_step.how: Go to a weekday morning tai chi class at the park, or email the group to ask about the next volunteer day.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome to tai chi, but gives no sign-up steps, and the class listing has no dates.

records.notes: Status is dormant because every dated item on the site is from 2005 to 2010 (founding, 2010 classes, a 2010 coastal cleanup). The tai chi listing has no dates and may be current, so confirm before a visit. The City list email (keeproyalgardensbeautiful@gmail.com) differs from the one on the site, and the site's address is used. The Morris Park address comes from the City list because the site does not publish one.

records.name: Sartain Street Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden on the City's Park Friends list, at 201 S Sartain St. We could not find a page that describes this garden.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City list gives the Washington Square West Civic Association community gardens page as this group's website (https://www.washwestcivic.org/community-gardens/, seen 2026-10-08). That page lists a 'Sartain Garden' at 1114 to 1118 Locust St and does not mention 201 S Sartain St, so it is not confirmed to be this garden. Nothing from that page is used in this record. The association's news links on that page are dated January 2023 and are not about this garden. The City list email is the stewardship office, not the group. Not searched further: the WebSearch budget was spent.

records.name: Friends of Saylor Grove Wetland
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Saylor Grove and the stormwater wetland that feeds Monoshone Creek. They keep the area clean and safe and run nature and art education programs.
records.what_you_do: Come to a spring or fall Love Your Park cleanup to weed, pick up litter, and help with a plant sale. Bird talks are often part of these days.

schedule.text: Love Your Park cleanups each spring and fall. The spring 2026 cleanup was on May 9, 2026, from 12 to 2 pm. The fall 2025 cleanup ran 10 am to noon. There is no weekly schedule.

locations.label: Saylor Grove wetland, W Rittenhouse St

first_step.how: Come to the next spring or fall Love Your Park cleanup. Follow the group on Facebook for the date, or send a message through the contact form on its blog.
first_step.basis: Cleanups are public events announced on the group's blog and Facebook page, and the blog has a contact form.

records.notes: The City list address is 669 W Rittenhouse St and the group's blog gives 720 W. Rittenhouse St, so no street number is shown until someone confirms it. The batch website had a www prefix that fails a certificate check, so the same blog without www was used. No email is published. The newest dated item is a post from April 2026 about a May 9, 2026 cleanup.

records.name: Friends of Schuylkill River Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Schuylkill River Park. They raise money and push for park upgrades, organize volunteer shifts, and host events such as a farmers market, basketball tournaments, and a fall festival.
records.what_you_do: Work a volunteer shift, look after one part of the park such as a dog run, the courts, or the gardens, support events, or serve on the board. Donations go to park projects.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts and events are posted on the events page. The fall 2026 tai chi session runs on Tuesdays from Sept 15 to Nov 24, 2026, with times that vary.

cost.text: No membership fee. Donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Sign up for a volunteer shift on the Get Involved page (fsrp.org/get-involved), or sign up for the newsletter on the contact page (fsrp.org/contact).
first_step.basis: The site invites the public to volunteer, lists its events publicly, and says how to sign up.

records.notes: The site's 2025 highlights are year only. The fall tai chi session has no year on the events page, but 2026 fits, since Sept 15, 2026 is a Tuesday. The farmers market listing (Sundays starting May 11) matches 2025, not 2026, so it may be out of date. The 2026 community survey is open. The 'What's New' page shows no dates.

records.name: The Friends of Sedgley Woods
records.summary: Volunteers who maintain Sedgley Woods, a 27-hole disc golf course in Fairmount Park. The group was founded in 1977 and runs the course's tournaments and weekly organized rounds.
records.what_you_do: Help with course upkeep at the second Saturday workday, or play in the monthly pro/am singles tournaments and the weekly tags. Play is free and the course is open to the public.

schedule.text: Workdays on the second Saturday of each month, 9 am to noon. Weekly tags on Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, with start times set by sunset on Thursday and at 11 am on Saturday and Sunday. Monthly pro/am singles tournaments. The course is open from sunup to sundown.

first_step.how: Come to a second Saturday workday, 9 am to noon, at the course, or email the group at friendsofsedgleywoods@gmail.com to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Workdays are open to volunteers and the site invites people to get in touch. No membership process is described.

records.notes: The group's dated items are year only: a 2026 board list and a link titled as the 2026 events schedule. That schedule document did not load, so no month is recorded. Status is active on the strength of the 2026 items. The vocabulary has no disc golf tag, so the group is filed under park care. The City list address (3400 Reservoir Dr) differs from the group's own address, which is used here. The site contains embedded text addressed to a reader or tool. It was ignored.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City list has no website, social page, or group email, only the stewardship office. Not searched: the WebSearch budget for this run was used on other groups.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The name points to the South Philadelphia Older Adult Center, but no source confirmed that link or who may use the garden, so no audience is recorded. Not searched: the WebSearch budget was spent. The City list email is the stewardship office, not the group.

records.name: Friends of Stephen Girard Park
records.summary: A neighbors' group for Stephen Girard Park in the Girard Estate area of South Philadelphia. A 2017 news article describes its monthly meetings and its part in the park's renovation plans. We found nothing newer.
records.what_you_do: The 2017 article describes a monthly meeting on a Wednesday evening, held inside the park's historic farmhouse. We found no newer details of what members do.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The newest dated source is a WHYY article published 2017-07-05, so the status is dormant. The group email comes from the City list and is not confirmed. A web search found no website or current contact for the group. The same article names the Girard Estate Neighbors Association, which is in leads_only.

records.name: Friends of Stinger Square
records.summary: Neighbors who help care for Stinger Square at 1400 S 32nd St. In May 2024 the group joined Parks and Recreation and partners for a spring cleanup and tree planting during Love Your Park Week.
records.what_you_do: Join a spring cleanup or planting day with the City and its partners. Past volunteer days included planting trees, collecting leaves for compost, and picking up litter.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The newest dated item is the City's release of 2024-05-10 about Love Your Park Week, so the status is dormant. No website or group email was found. The City list email is the stewardship office. A single search for this group and Thomas Hart Park found no current page for either.

records.name: Friends of Tacony Creek Park
records.summary: Neighbors and visitors who look after Tacony Creek Park, a 300-acre watershed park in lower Northeast Philadelphia. The group runs free group walks and runs on the trails.
records.what_you_do: Join a free group walk or run on the trails, or volunteer to help care for the land. The volunteer page explains how to sign up.

schedule.text: Weekly group walks and runs, called Walk with Me and Run with Me, plus other trail programs. The site does not list days or times.

first_step.how: Sign up through the volunteer page (friendsoftaconycreekpark.org/volunteer/), or send a question through the contact page (friendsoftaconycreekpark.org/contact-us/).
first_step.basis: The site describes its members as neighbors and people who spend time in the park, says its trail programs are free, and lists a volunteer page and a contact page. Sign-up details are not on the page.

records.notes: The batch name, Tacony Creek Park Keepers, now appears as Friends of Tacony Creek Park, and tcpkeepers.org redirects to the new site. The site lists no dated events or news, so status is probably active based on its recurring programs. The partnership's events calendar (ttfwatershed.org/events/) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The City list has a staff email at the watershed partnership, which the group's site does not publish, so it is not used. The City list has no street address, so none is given. The City list entry 'Friends of Whitaker' gives the same park name.

records.name: Friends of Whitaker
records.summary: A Friends group the City lists under Whitaker, with Tacony Creek Park as its other name. We could not find a page for it.

locations.label: Whitaker (City list also names Tacony Creek Park)

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City list gives no website and no street address. Its other name, Tacony Creek Park, matches the entry for Tacony Creek Park Keepers (city_friends:836), which has its own website. It may be the same group or a second group for that park. Not checked: the WebSearch budget was spent. The City list email is the stewardship office.

records.name: Friends of the Rail Park
records.summary: A nonprofit building a three-mile greenway from old rail tracks, in three sections across ten neighborhoods from Northern Liberties to Fairmount Park. The park is free and open every day, and volunteers help with clean-ups and green-ups.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer clean-up or green-up, take a tour of the park, or become a member. The October 2026 clean-up is Wed Oct 14 and the green-up is Wed Oct 21.

schedule.text: The park is open daily, 7 am to 10 pm. Upcoming in 2026: a park tour and a hip hop dance event on Sat Oct 10, the October clean-up on Wed Oct 14, the green-up on Wed Oct 21, and a Furry Friends tour on Sat Oct 24.

cost.text: Free to visit. Membership and donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the Oct 14 volunteer clean-up on the events page (therailpark.org/news-and-events), or book a tour through the site's Book a Tour page.
first_step.basis: Clean-ups and tours are listed publicly with dates, and the site gives a way to sign up.

records.notes: The newest evidence is a list of events dated October 2026, which shows the group is running programs now. The City list email matches the one on the group's site. The group also lists a mailing PO Box and a Spanish and a Chinese version of its site, which are not recorded here.

records.name: The Spring Gardens
records.summary: A volunteer-run community garden that neighbors started in 1995 in the Spring Garden area. Members grow food and flowers, and the garden also runs cooking workshops, gardening classes, school tours, and bike tours.
records.what_you_do: Garden members, who live inside the garden's boundaries, grow a plot. Volunteers sign up through a GivePulse page linked from the site. The garden also hosts events such as a yoga class and food truck nights.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the events calendar. Recent examples: a yoga class on Sept 28, 2026 (6:30 to 7:30 pm) and Parks on Tap, Sept 16 to 20, 2026. Garden hours are not on the site.

cost.text: Membership and class prices are not stated. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Join the waitlist for a garden plot on the site's waitlist page, or sign up to volunteer through the group's GivePulse page.
first_step.basis: Plots are for residents inside the garden's boundaries and there is a waitlist. Volunteer sign-up is public.

records.notes: The batch name 'The Spring Gardeners' appears on the group's site as 'The Spring Gardens', which this record uses. The address 1828 North St comes from the City list and is not on the site, which gives only a PO Box (19130). Kind is set to garden because the group runs a community garden.

records.name: Friends of Thomas Hart Park
records.summary: A Friends group the City lists for Thomas Hart Park at 1321 N 4th St. We could not find a web page or current source for it.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

notes: All 15 batch groups have a record; all are publish. Searches: 3 of 3 used (Stephen Girard Park; Roots Garden in Fisher Park; Stinger Square combined with Thomas Hart Park). Not searched because the budget ran out: South Street Community Garden, SPOAC community garden, Friends of Whitaker, and Sartain Street Community Garden. The City's Park Friends list page on phila.gov has no per-group details, only the stewardship office. Friends of Saylor Grove's site uses a different street number than the City list (see its record). The Sartain record's City-listed website is a civic association page that does not name this garden. Not added to leads_only: Washington Square West Civic Association (washwestcivic.org), whose gardens page was read for the Sartain record and is a civic group for a later pass; Olney Culture Lab (olneyculturelab.org), the maker of the Roots Garden documentary. Sedgley Woods' site contained embedded text aimed at a reader or tool, which was ignored. Status counts: active 5, probably_active 1, dormant 3, unknown 6.
